title: A.J. Brown finally gets going, and other takeaways from Day 5 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: A.J. Brown excelled in the Patriots' first padded practice, showing strong chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye.
Christian Gonzalez participated fully in practice despite ongoing contract negotiations, performing well in drills and scrimmages.
DeAndre Hopkins' brief coaching stint with the Patriots ended; Hopkins has not officially retired from playing in the NFL.

title: Child on bike injured in crash with SUV in Wellesley
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Child on bike suffers potentially serious injuries in crash with SUV at Wellesley's Oakland Street and Woodlawn Avenue.
The child was conscious and alert, transported to Boston hospital for evaluation; SUV driver stayed on scene.
Wellesley Police Crash Reconstruction Unit investigates; Oakland Street closed temporarily but now reopened.

title: Where to go in New England this August
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: The Milford Oyster Festival in Connecticut happens Aug. 14-15, featuring music, food, rides, and local oysters.
The Foreside Inn, a new boutique hotel, opened in Kittery, Maine, close to shops and downtown Portsmouth, N.H.
Dine Out Boston runs Aug. 1-15, offering multi-course lunch and dinner menus at set prices; includes three Saturdays.

title: Investigation underway after 2 found dead along same stretch of Mass. river
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two bodies were recovered days apart along the Connecticut River stretch in Western Massachusetts, according to authorities.
21-year-old Hermes Mariano Almonte of Worcester was found drowned near Rock Dam, no foul play suspected.
An unidentified adult male was found deceased near Smead Island; investigations are ongoing by state and local police.

title: Federal investigation finds Burlington schools violated the law over ‘graphic’ student survey
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Burlington Public Schools violated federal law by forcing students to take a survey with sensitive sexual questions.
The U.S. Department of Education says the district ignored parental opt-out requests for the 2025 survey.
The district will update policies, issue apologies, and submit future surveys for federal review to comply with regulations.

title: Pedestrian struck by vehicle on Cape Cod has died
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A pedestrian struck by a vehicle last Saturday in Chatham has died, according to local police.
The collision occurred on Route 28 near Crosby Lane in West Chatham at around 7:50 a.m.
The driver remained at the scene, and the incident is still under investigation by Chatham Police.

title: Vrabel: Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas is getting closer to participating in training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas is nearing a return after recovering from a knee procedure and recent contract signing.
Jacas is on the non-football injury list, preventing him from practice; Patriots can activate him anytime.
Head coach Mike Vrabel anticipates Jacas may return soon, unlike veteran Harold Landry, who remains sidelined.

title: Wondering how to fit that 48-oz. iced coffee in your car? Don’t worry, Dunkin’ has got you
author: Peter Chianca
bullets: Dunkin' is reintroducing its 48-ounce 'Iced Beverage Bucket' with a new cup holder available for $12.
The 'Iced Beverage Bucket Holder' is designed to fit into standard car cup holders, but it is currently sold out.
The 48-ounce coffee bucket will be available again at Dunkin' starting Aug. 7 for $12.99 including the beverage.

title: Get the ultimate New England summer travel guide
author: Zipporah Osei
bullets: Boston.com offers Summer Six newsletter with travel tips for Boston and New England.
Newsletter includes top beach towns, Cape Cod activities, and scenic hikes.
Features local eateries and hidden gems with insights into iconic New England experiences.

title: First responders detail scene at Duxbury home on Day 3 of Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: First responders described a chaotic scene and life-saving efforts at the Clancy home during Lindsay Clancy's murder trial.
Firefighter testimonies detailed attempts to resuscitate the Clancy children, who were found unresponsive on January 24, 2023.
Duxbury police officers testified about finding Lindsay Clancy injured and unresponsive children in the basement on the trial's third day.
